steps.text: JavaScript shows text with console.log(). Text goes inside quote marks. Press Run!
What will this print?
steps.explanation: console.log() shows the text inside the quotes, without the quote marks.

steps.text: Each console.log() prints on a new line.
Type exactly what this prints.
steps.explanation: Every console.log() starts a new line.

steps.text: This code has a bug. Fix line 1 so it prints Hello.
steps.hint: Text needs a quote mark at the start AND at the end.
steps.explanation: A string must be closed with a second quote mark: "Hello".

steps.text: Your turn! Print: I love coding
steps.hint: Use console.log() with the words inside quote marks.

lessons.title: Playing with text
lessons.objective: Join text with + and repeat it with .repeat().

steps.text: The + sign joins two pieces of text.
What will this print?
steps.explanation: + glues the strings together with nothing in between: catfish.

steps.text: .repeat(n) repeats text n times.
Type exactly what this prints.
steps.explanation: "Go! " repeated twice is "Go! Go! ".

steps.text: JavaScript is fussy about capital letters. Fix line 1.
steps.hint: console starts with a small c.
steps.explanation: JavaScript knows console with a small c. Console with a capital C is an unknown name.

steps.text: Join "Hari " and "Raya" with + so it prints: Hari Raya
steps.hint: Put both strings inside console.log() with a + between them.

lessons.title: Variables
lessons.objective: Store values in variables with let.

steps.text: let makes a variable: a labelled box for a value.
What will this print?
steps.explanation: Quote marks make "city" plain text, so the word city is printed.

steps.text: A let variable can change. The newest value wins.
Type exactly what this prints.
steps.explanation: food is changed from "roti" to "satay" before it is printed.

steps.text: Line 2 has a typo in the variable name. Fix it.
steps.hint: Check the spelling of the variable on line 1.
steps.explanation: The variable is called name. nam is a name JavaScript has never seen.

steps.text: Finish the program so it prints: My pet is a cat
steps.solution:
let pet = "cat";
console.log("My pet is a " + pet);
steps.hint: Join "My pet is a " and pet with +.

lessons.title: Putting it together
lessons.objective: Combine text and variables to make messages.

steps.text: Join variables and text to build a full name. The " " adds a space.
Careful! These numbers are inside quotes. What will this print?
steps.explanation: With quotes they are text, and + joins text, so you get 12.

steps.text: A comma in console.log() prints things with a space between them.
Type exactly what this prints.
steps.explanation: The comma prints both values with one space between them.

steps.text: Line 2 is missing something between the text and the variable. Fix it.
steps.hint: Use + (or a comma) to join two things.
steps.explanation: JavaScript needs a + or a comma between "Hello " and friend.

steps.text: Finish the program so it prints: Welcome to Melaka!
steps.hint: Join "Welcome to ", town and "!".

steps.text: JavaScript is a calculator too. / can give a decimal answer.
What will this print?
steps.explanation: Multiplication happens first: 3 * 4 is 12, then 12 - 2 is 10.

steps.text: Math.floor() drops the decimal part. % gives the remainder.
Type exactly what this prints.
steps.explanation: 20 cakes shared by 6 friends: each gets 3, and 2 are left over.

steps.text: This should print the total cost as a number. Fix line 2.
steps.hint: Numbers have no quote marks.
steps.explanation: "10" with quotes is text, so + joins instead of adding.

steps.text: A pizza has 8 slices and you eat 3. Print how many are left, using a calculation.
steps.hint: Subtract eaten from slices inside console.log().

lessons.title: Comparing things
lessons.objective: Use comparisons that answer true or false.

steps.text: Comparisons answer true or false. === checks if two things are equal.
What will this print?
steps.explanation: <= means "less than or equal to". 10 equals 10, so it is true.

steps.text: You can compare text too. Capital letters matter!
Type exactly what this prints.
steps.explanation: 12 is not 13 or more, so the answer is false.

steps.text: Line 2 should compare, not store. Fix it.
steps.hint: Use === to compare.
steps.explanation: A single = stores a value. Comparing needs ===.

steps.text: Print whether 7 is greater than 4 (it should print true).
steps.hint: Put a comparison with > inside console.log().

lessons.title: Making choices with if
lessons.objective: Run code only when a condition is true.

steps.text: if runs the code in { } only when the condition in ( ) is true.
What will this print?
steps.explanation: 45 is less than 50, so the else part runs.

steps.text: else runs when the condition is false.
Type exactly what this prints.
steps.explanation: 4 % 2 is 0, so the number is even.

steps.text: Line 2 is missing brackets around the condition. Fix it.
steps.hint: The condition goes inside ( ).
steps.explanation: JavaScript needs round brackets around an if condition.

steps.text: Finish the program: if hour is less than 12, print Selamat pagi, otherwise print Selamat petang.
steps.hint: Use if (hour < 12) { ... } else { ... }.

lessons.title: More choices with else if
lessons.objective: Choose between more than two paths.

steps.text: else if is checked only when the conditions above were false.
What will this print?
steps.explanation: The first condition that is true wins: 120 > 110.

steps.text: && needs both sides true. || needs at least one.
Type exactly what this prints.
steps.explanation: x is neither more nor less than 0, so the else part runs.

steps.text: Line 4 should check another condition. Fix it.
steps.hint: else cannot have a condition; use else if.
steps.explanation: Only else if can have its own condition.

steps.text: Finish the program to print Hot above 30, Warm above 20, and Cool otherwise.
steps.hint: Use if, else if and else in that order.

lessons.title: Loops with for
lessons.objective: Repeat code with a for loop.

steps.text: This for loop counts i from 0 while i < 3, adding 1 each time.
steps.expected_output:
Hip hip hooray!
Hip hip hooray!
Hip hip hooray!

steps.text: What will this print?
steps.explanation: i takes the values 0, 1, 2 and 3, so the loop runs four times and count ends at 4.

steps.text: Start the counter wherever you like.
Type exactly what this prints.
steps.explanation: i takes the values 1, 2 and 3.

steps.text: This loop should run 2 times. Fix line 1.
steps.hint: The counter has to go up to reach 2.
steps.explanation: i-- makes i go down, so it never reaches 2 and the loop never ends. i++ counts up.

steps.text: Use a for loop to print Hello 3 times.

lessons.title: Loops with while
lessons.objective: Repeat while a condition stays true.

steps.text: while repeats as long as its condition is true. Change the counter, or it never stops!
What will this print?
steps.explanation: n goes 10, 6, 2, -2. Now n > 0 is false, so the loop stops and -2 is printed.

steps.text: A loop can keep a running total.
Type exactly what this prints.
steps.explanation: x becomes 3, then 9, then 27. 27 is not below 20, so the loop stops.

steps.text: This loop never ends. Fix line 4 so the counter goes up.
steps.hint: The counter must change each time round.
steps.explanation: i never changed, so i < 3 stayed true forever.

steps.text: Use a while loop to print 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 (one per line).
steps.hint: Keep going while n > 0, and take 1 away each time.

lessons.title: Arrays
lessons.objective: Keep many values in one array.

steps.text: An array holds many values in square brackets. Positions start at 0!
What will this print?
steps.explanation: Positions start at 0, so [1] is the second item: green.

steps.text: push() adds an item to the end. join() turns the array into text.
Type exactly what this prints.
steps.explanation: nums[2] is 15 and nums[0] is 4, so the sum is 19.

steps.text: This array has 3 items, so the last position is 2. Fix line 2.
steps.hint: The last position is one less than the length.
steps.explanation: There is no position 3: the positions are 0, 1 and 2.

steps.text: Add "teh tarik" to drinks with push, then print drinks.join(", ").
steps.hint: Use drinks.push(...) and then print drinks.join(", ").
